summary: This excerpt from Book 4 (part 114) follows Valentine in a famine-stricken, war-scarred city. Her mother returns from three weeks in hospital with mended bones, and the family shares a meagre dinner and a painkiller. Valentine cannot sleep, takes a glowing light from her galosh on a secret night walk, and reflects on the worsening bread rations and the hunger that pride cannot cure. The passage ends mid-scene as a man snatches her bread in the queue.
one_line: Valentine's mother returns from hospital to a starving, war-torn city, and Valentine's hunger and pride are tested in the bread queue.
key_facts: Valentine's mother came home after three weeks in hospital, where she had her broken bones mended.
Valentine's mother walked into the flat like an old woman and hobbled across the room to hug Valentine.
Valentine's brother Trover, who had been silent, got up from the table and hugged both of them.
Trover was now tall enough to hug Valentine at the waist instead of the knees.
Her mother ate some of the dinner and took a painkiller in pill form, which were now everywhere.
Under Valentine's bed was the remains of her grip sheet parcel, including one winter galosh; the other had been stolen the winter before.
A pea-sized glowing light was kept in the toe of the galosh, which Valentine had never considered selling for bread.
Valentine took the glowing light outside on a secret walk through the old streets of the city during the hot night.
Nine months after her father died, winter had sent autumn as a threatening envoy.
The bread ration had been cut to 120 grams, and pebbles were sometimes found in the bread to increase its weight.
Valentine and the other diggers cursed the enemy, not the city, when the bread was bad.
Valentine was so hungry all the time, and the narrator notes that you couldn't eat pride.
In the bread queue, a man old enough to be her father snatched her ration from her trembling hands.
